A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FREE-Merging research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-E support reliable comparison, including matching content across changed pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-merging experiments across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, together with ablations and supplementary analyses in appendices D-E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a router-training-data ablation in Appendix D.6 and Table 13.

M1.justification: Fourier filtering, merging coefficients, expert extraction and rescaling, and dynamic routing remain unchanged in Equations 1-4 and Algorithm 1. The added router analysis does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same vision, language, and multimodal datasets and tasks. The new router ablation uses the existing eight visual tasks; the added forgetting discussion introduces no evaluated task.

E2.justification: Matched comparison tables and figures retain their comparator sets. The newly cited Fuse to Forget work is discussed but not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: New Table 13 evaluates router-training fractions of 0%, 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, and 5% on the existing eight-task vision setup. Other protocols remain unchanged. The table labels the models ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14, although D.6 inconsistently calls the latter ViT-B/14.

E4.justification: v2 D.6 explains the router's role without testing its training-data requirements. v3 adds this sensitivity analysis in Table 13. Existing component, sparsity, random-router, filtering-frequency, and loss-landscape analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New Table 13 continues point-estimate reporting. Frequency-domain amplitude variance remains an interference measure, not a newly introduced uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: New Table 13 reports accuracies of 87.0/92.1 at 0.1% router-training data, 89.7/93.7 at 1%, and 90.1/94.1 at 5% for ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14, respectively. These are additional budget-dependent results; all matched pre-existing table values and figure findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1, its Appendix B proof, and the mathematical definitions and derivations are unchanged. The new forgetting discussion introduces no formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about frequency-domain interference, the backbone-plus-experts approach, and performance-cost trade-offs across domains. Editorial rewording does not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: New D.8 explains that forgetting can be desirable for reducing bias or undesirable information, distinguishing that objective from this paper's capability preservation. D.6 interprets the new ablation as supporting a 1% router-training budget, with 0.1% suggested under tighter resource constraints.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and newly documents using 1% of the data for router training. v2 provides neither disclosure. Hardware information remains unchanged; the newly stated training fraction does not establish that earlier experiments used a different setting.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zaman et al.'s Fuse to Forget as reference 54 and discusses its selective-forgetting objective in new Appendix D.8. This provides a limited extension of research positioning; the remaining cited works and relationships are retained.

P1.justification: v3 tightens portions of the introduction and related work, expands Appendix E and future-work prose, and inserts D.8 before the renamed D.9 future-work section. It also adds a corresponding-author designation and acknowledgements. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds router-ablation Table 13, moves table captions above their tables, removes printed page numbers, and rearranges appendix displays. For example, the 30-task results move from Table 14 to Table 16. Existing figures retain their graphics without redrawing.

improvement.justification: Table 13 supplies practical evidence missing from v2 for choosing the router-training budget, while the disclosed 1% setting and code link improve reproducibility information. New D.8 usefully clarifies when forgetting is desirable. These are limited gains: the method and prior results remain unchanged, and the new ablation lacks uncertainty estimates and contains a model-name inconsistency between D.6 and Table 13.
